human_actions_pending.action: Choose whether Phase B's mapper is reflection-based or source-generated
human_actions_pending.context: Reflection is simpler and works with types unknown at compile time; source generation is what MemoryPack and System.Text.Json use, and is required for Native AOT and trimming. Note the distinction already drawn: reading a known type's properties is fine, resolving an attacker-supplied name to a type is not, and the codec still never does the latter.

decisions.decision: Type byte splits into a shape nibble and a type nibble
decisions.rationale: The high nibble says how to skip a frame, so a fixed-width value needs no Length and an unknown type is still skippable. Dropping Length without it would cost the property that makes unknown frames survive.

decisions.decision: Shapes 0xB_ to 0xE_ can never be allocated
decisions.rationale: They carry no width, so a reader written today could not skip them. Allocating them later would be exactly the ossification the split exists to prevent.

decisions.decision: Unknown types are preserved, not rejected
decisions.rationale: The shape says how far the frame reaches, so it decodes opaque and re-encodes byte-for-byte. Matches what TYPED already did for unknown type names; RFC 8949 5.4 makes the same point about unknown CBOR tags.

decisions.decision: A schema mode must never drop the type byte, only fold the shape into the field tag
decisions.rationale: Dropping it drops the shape, and an unknown field stops being something a reader steps over and becomes something that silently desynchronises the rest. Protobuf carries three bits of wire type in its tag for this reason. User directive: stay on the safe side.

decisions.decision: The codec never maps a type name to a System.Type
decisions.rationale: BinaryFormatter was removed from .NET 9 over this. Avro shipped three versions of one allow-list before it held, and MessagePack-CSharp's failed to recurse into generic arguments. A decoder with no code path that constructs cannot be argued into constructing.

decisions.decision: Only the shortest varint encoding is legal, and values must fit in 64 bits
decisions.rationale: Otherwise a document has more than one valid byte representation: re-encoding stops being byte-exact, and where bytes are hashed or signed it is the BER/DER signature-bypass shape.

decisions.decision: NaN is canonicalised per width; negative zero is preserved
decisions.rationale: Every NaN payload would otherwise be a separate encoding of one value. -0.0 is a different value, not a different spelling, since 1/-0.0 is negative infinity.

decisions.decision: TEXT_ONCE kept after measurement, having first been reverted
decisions.rationale: Costs an extra traversal and about 2x encode time on long repeated text, but saves 196 bytes on values-mixed and cuts encode allocation 28-68% on four shapes. The allocation half was missed in the first recommendation and surfaced only when the revert was measured.

decisions.decision: Every TEXT frame claims a value id, counted by literal rather than by distinct value
decisions.rationale: The decoder appends one entry per literal. Counting distinct values instead stalls on the second literal of a short value and every later id lands one out — a fault that leaves the document well-formed and silently resolves references to the wrong string.
A reference costs three bytes and a small integer costs two, so it could only lose. Revisit only for repeated GUIDs or hashes, and only with a measurement.

decisions.decision: PrimitiveKind is public; TlvType stays internal
decisions.rationale: The prototype exposed a public raw Type byte with an internal vocabulary, so no caller outside the assembly could read a value. Callers switch on meaning, not on a wire detail.

decisions.decision: Solo git-flow, no pull requests; main fast-forwarded to develop, no version tags
decisions.rationale: User works alone. Local hooks block direct commits on main and develop, so every change needs a feature branch.

next_action: Nothing is in flight. Phase B is the natural next step and needs a design before any code — the open question is reflection versus source generation. Do not start it without the user asking.
context_notes: The working loop: settle a format question in conversation, write the reasoning into docs/, implement against the doc, measure with the exact instruments, then fold findings back into docs/tlv-performance.md. Docs lead code, and when measurement contradicts a doc the doc gets corrected — that has now happened four times and every correction was worth it. Verification is not optional here: checking has found a real defect every single time it was applied, including two this session that no existing test caught.
